thread:
ellie: Heads-up: p95 decode jumped ~18% on canary after yesterday's attn-kernel merge. Not in prod yet but canary shows a consistent shift. Sharing quick flame and perf output below.

ci-bot: CI perf: decode_p95 increased 22% on e2e-perf-canary run #4021. https://ci.redwood.company/runs/4021 :warning:

ellie: perf top (sampled) from the canary instance:```
attn_kernel_select()         35%
matmul_fuse_path()           28%
decode_loop()                18%
kv_cache_lookup()            10%
other                        9%
```

noah: Which merge? the attn arbitration one?

dmitri: That would be PR 5234 yes — we flipped the selector to prefer the fused matmul path for shortseqs to improve throughput.

ellie: Right. Quick microbench I ran: shortseq (seq=8/16) p95 regressed a lot; longseq (seq>=64) unchanged. Also saw KV cache hit-rate dip ~2.3% on canary (weird).

cara: Hypothesis: fused path raises SM occupancy / changes prefetch timing -> memory-copy interleaving with KV prefetch causes stalls on the decode hotpath. Need traces (nvprof/nsight) and a kernel-choice breakdown per request.

noah: Suggest bisecting the selector change. If we revert the arbitration tweak and p95 goes back, that pins it. I can run a quick git-bisect on the staging branch.

ellie: I already did a light bisect locally. Reverting the selector flip removes the regression in my small repro. But we need full canary confirm.

cara: Run this trace on the failing config:```
./bin/infer_bench --model=gpt-small --seq=16 --batch=2 --trace=nvprof --kv-prefetch=on --profile-interval=10s
```
That will capture SM utilization + memcpy overlap.

infra-bot: Canary hold placed on rollout 2025-07-12T09:12Z by cara — reason: p95 decode regression on canary.

dmitri: I'm preparing a rollback PR (r-5240) that reverts the selector heuristic. If that fixes canary perf we'll cut a hotpatch.

ellie: Action items: 1) dmitri run canary with rollback PR 2) noah produce microbench matrix for seq {8,16,32,64} x batch {1,2,4} 3) cara collect nvprof traces and compare memcpy timelines 4) infra keep rollout on hold until we have canary result.

noah: Starting the matrix now, ETA ~45m. I'll post a small CSV of p95 deltas.

(later)

noah: Matrix results posted: seq=8 p95 +42% vs baseline, seq=16 +31%, seq=32 +4%, seq=64 ~0%. CSV: https://perf.redwood.company/matrix/1739456789.csv

dmitri: Rollback PR r-5240 opened and deployed to canary. Running the canary perf job now.

ci-bot: Canary perf job #4030 completed. decode_p95 delta: -2% (regression removed). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.company/runs/4030

ellie: Confirming from canary logs: rollback removes the p95 spike. Selector was routing a surprisingly-high fraction of shortseq requests to fused_matmul path which, under our KV-prefetch timing, increased tail latency.

cara: Follow-ups: add an integration test that measures chosen-kernel distribution per seq length and asserts latency-regression < 10% when selector changes. Also add a lightweight telemetry metric: kernel_choice_ratio{seq_len, model, kernel} emitted to metrics so we can detect sudden shifts automatically.

dmitri: Agreed. I'll prepare the hotpatch (revert + rebaseline) and the test. Also will add a small heuristic patch: penalize fused path if kv_prefetch_score > threshold.

ellie: Great. I'll open the postmortem template and attach perf graphs, nvprof timelines, and the microbench CSV. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :heart:

cara: +1 on postmortem and the telemetry. Also add a note to the rollout playbook: "when kernel choice changes, run shortseq microbench before broad rollout."

ellie: Closing the loop here — canary hold remains until hotpatch merges and CI rebaselines. I'll update the release ticket.

ci-bot: Note: remember to re-run the e2e perf baseline after hotpatch to refresh expectations.
